transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m convinced a former client has quietly used my ideas to structure things so I’m being pushed out of my own field, and I can’t be talked out of that belief. A younger colleague I mentor suggested I come in for an evaluation, but I know what is happening is real.
Can you tell me more about how you came to believe that your former client is behind this plot to push you out of your field, and what evidence you have to support this belief?

This all started about eleven months ago, right after I finished a major advisory contract with this client, and my consulting referrals suddenly dried up completely. I am certain they copied my proprietary frameworks into their internal playbook and used their industry influence to nudge others to stop sending me work. Some try to tell me it's just a normal slowdown from semi-retirement, but that explanation is simply implausible given the precise timing.
Have you experienced any periods over the past eleven months where you doubted this belief about your former client, or has it remained constant and unshakeable the entire time?

It has remained completely constant and unshakeable for the entire eleven months; I haven't doubted it for a single moment. Even though my colleague and others keep trying to tell me it's just a normal slowdown from my semi-retirement, I am absolutely sure there is no other logical explanation for how suddenly my referrals stopped.
Have you taken any actions or made significant decisions based on this belief about your former client, such as confronting them or changing your business practices in response?

I haven't confronted the client directly, but I have made the decision to turn down several potential collaborations and referrals from anyone connected to their network. I do this because I'm convinced those offers are just part of the effort to edge me out, which has ended up narrowing my consulting opportunities much more than my semi-retirement plans originally would have.

Have you experienced any other beliefs or ideas that you're absolutely certain of, but others around you, including friends, family, or colleagues, think are not true or are exaggerated, aside from this situation with your former client?

No, there is absolutely nothing else like that. Outside of this specific situation with my former client, my daily life and thinking are completely normal. No one has ever questioned any other aspect of my beliefs, and I manage my household, my painting, and my finances just as I always have.
Have you experienced any hallucinations, such as hearing or seeing things that others cannot, or have you only been dealing with this persistent belief about your former client?

No, I have never experienced any hallucinations or seen and heard things that aren't there. My mind is perfectly clear, and the only thing I am dealing with is the absolute certainty that my former client is actively working to sideline me from my field.

Have you experienced any significant changes in your emotional state, such as depression, anxiety, or irritability, specifically in relation to this belief about your former client, or have you remained emotionally stable throughout this period?

I haven't really experienced any significant emotional changes like depression, anxiety, or irritability over this past year. Aside from my ongoing concern about this situation with my former client, I feel emotionally stable and continue to go about my daily life as usual.

Can you think of any evidence, no matter how small, that could potentially prove your belief about your former client wrong, or is it impossible for you to consider that you might be mistaken about their involvement?

It is simply impossible for me to consider that I might be mistaken about their involvement. I cannot see any other plausible explanation for why my referrals dried up so abruptly right after that specific contract ended. No matter what others say about this being a normal, age-related slowdown, I remain absolutely convinced of this client's deliberate role.

Have you ever had a period where you had two or more of the following: hallucinations, disorganized speech, catatonic behavior, or disorganized or abnormal motor behavior, that lasted for at least a month?

No, I have never experienced any of those things. I've never had hallucinations, disorganized speech, or any unusual physical behaviors. My thinking and speech have always remained perfectly clear and normal.
